name: Kiln-fired brick in Mesopotamia
summary: Kiln-fired brick, harder and more durable than sun-dried mud brick, was familiar in Mesopotamian building from the Early Dynastic period, about 3000 to 2300 BCE.
description: Baked brick, moulded from tempered mud and fired to hardness in a kiln, was familiar in Mesopotamian architecture from the Early Dynastic period, about 3000 to 2300 BCE. It was more durable than sun-dried brick. In neighbouring Iran it came into use in monumental buildings only in the 2nd millennium BCE.

impact.note: Scored on the general view, not on the cited page: baked brick descending from Mesopotamian practice was used across Western Asia for millennia, but the Indus and Chinese fired bricks may be separate lines, so reach is held at 2; it improved on mud brick rather than creating a new way of building (depth 1) and had a few direct successors such as glazed brick (generativity 1).

date.label: Early Dynastic period, c. 3000–2300 BCE
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Kiln-fired brick was familiar in Mesopotamian architecture from the Early Dynastic period, about 3000 to 2300 BCE.

evidence.supports: fired to hardness in a kiln, though familiar in Mesopotamian architecture from the Early Dynastic period (ca. 3000-2300 b.c.; Delougaz; Eaton-Francis, p. 5), came into use in monumental structures in Iran only in the 2nd millennium b.c.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: Find excavation reports for the earliest kiln-fired bricks in Mesopotamia (Uruk-period and earlier use is claimed) and at Chengtoushan (Hunan), c. 4400 BCE.
The standardised fired brick of the Indus cities from c. 2600 BCE may be independent and deserves its own record.

research.note: The Iranica article does not say where kiln-fired brick first appeared, and earlier claims elsewhere were not checked, so the evidence does not settle whether Mesopotamia was first or independent.
